_readme: Diverse companion_router scenarios for Felix to review (29 Sep). Not wired into pytest yet — a reviewable set first. Each entry has a conversation history, the user's turn, and what the router SHOULD do. 'verified' scenarios were actually run against the real LLM tonight (n=20 each, see #36's record); 'untested' ones are proposed additions covering gaps in tonight's coverage. Once reviewed, this becomes the seed for an automated replay suite so a future prompt change can be checked against the whole set at once instead of one case at a time.

scenarios.description: User names an activity outright.
scenarios.user_input: I want to do the Extended Fitness Check-in
scenarios.status: verified (base case, used throughout tonight's replays)

scenarios.description: Unambiguous yes right after the router listed activities.
scenarios.prior_assistant: There are a few things we could do together: the Fitness Check-in or a focus group. What interests you?
scenarios.user_input: the fitness one

scenarios.description: User answers the question the running activity just asked. The router should NOT re-fire — currently it does, 20/20, across 4 prompt variants (buried-in-history, more-history+brief, dedicated-line+full, dedicated-line+brief). Root cause writeup on #36's record.
scenarios.prior_assistant: Okay. I'm Grace... May I ask what you're called?
scenarios.user_input: My name is Felix
scenarios.status: verified failing — 80/80 trials wrongly called start_activity

scenarios.description: User explicitly asks to redo the activity that's already running — this SHOULD fire, per the router's own stated rule ('only call start_activity again if they clearly ask to restart').
scenarios.user_input: actually can we start that over from the beginning
scenarios.status: untested — no replay has checked the 'restart' carve-out actually works, only that the ordinary continuation case wrongly fires

scenarios.description: User asks for a DIFFERENT activity while one is already running. Undefined behavior today — should this end the current one and start the new one, or refuse until they explicitly leave first? Worth deciding before it comes up live.
scenarios.user_input: actually let's do the memory game instead
scenarios.expect: UNDECIDED — flagging for review, not a bug report

scenarios.description: Activity name appears in the sentence but isn't a request.
scenarios.user_input: my neighbor said she liked the fitness check-in thing you do

scenarios.description: A bare 'sure' with nothing offered this session yet — must not start anything (mirrors the existing 'sure doesn't silently restart' precedent).
scenarios.user_input: sure

scenarios.description: Unambiguous stop request.
scenarios.user_input: actually let's stop this

scenarios.description: Mood word that answers the question just asked, not a stop request.
scenarios.prior_assistant: How have you been feeling about your fitness routine?
scenarios.user_input: not so good

scenarios.description: A real, on-topic reason someone might want to stop, but not an explicit request to.
scenarios.user_input: my knees have been bothering me
scenarios.expect: no tool (borderline — currently abstains after tonight's tool-description change; flagged to Felix as a judgment call, not settled)
scenarios.status: verified 0/20 in the latest build, was 20/20 before a wording change — worth re-checking after any future prompt edit

scenarios.description: 'Stop' used about something other than the activity.
scenarios.user_input: can you stop asking so many questions at once
scenarios.status: untested — plausible false-positive on the word 'stop' alone

scenarios.description: Very short, ambiguous reply with no content.
scenarios.user_input: hm

scenarios.description: Stop request phrased as a question rather than a statement.
scenarios.user_input: could we maybe stop for today?

scenarios.description: The stop request is real but embedded in an otherwise on-topic answer.
scenarios.prior_assistant: How often do you exercise per week?
scenarios.user_input: usually three times, but honestly I'd rather stop for today

scenarios.description: Direct question about what's available.
scenarios.user_input: what could we do?
scenarios.status: verified (used as the base offer case throughout tonight)

scenarios.description: Indirect signal of wanting something to do.
scenarios.user_input: I don't know, I'm a bit bored

scenarios.description: Two intents in one turn: leave this one AND see what else there is. Router can only call one tool — which should win, and does the reply's own wording cover the other half?
scenarios.user_input: I don't want to do this anymore, what else is there?
scenarios.expect: UNDECIDED — likely end_activity first (leaving takes priority), reply should offer to list afterward

scenarios.description: Clear yes to 'Shall we stop X?'
scenarios.user_input: yes, let's stop

scenarios.description: Clear no.
scenarios.user_input: no, let's keep going

scenarios.description: Off-topic / doesn't answer the yes-no question.
scenarios.user_input: what were we talking about again?

scenarios.description: A bare 'yes' that reads naturally as answering something else entirely, not the stop question — checks whether the narrow check is actually reading the confirmation question in context or just pattern-matching 'yes'.
scenarios.prior_assistant: Shall we stop the fitness check-in? By the way, did you want water after this?
scenarios.user_input: yes please
scenarios.expect: genuinely ambiguous — worth seeing what it does, not a known-good answer

scenarios.description: The exact #36 reproduction, but in German — checks whether the bug is language-specific or general (Felix's live test that found it WAS in German).
scenarios.prior_assistant: Okay. Ich bin Grace... Darf ich erfahren, wie du heißt?
scenarios.user_input: Ich heiße Felix
scenarios.status: verified failing — this is the literal turn from Felix's live test tonight

scenarios.description: Mid-sentence language switch — checks the router isn't thrown by it.
scenarios.user_input: ich möchte eigentlich just stop for now

scenarios.description: User says something close to but not exactly an activity's title — checks the router resolves to the right one rather than guessing wrong or refusing.
scenarios.user_input: let's do the grace group thing
